summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, asthma, and a history of substance use was admitted after being found altered at home following heavy alcohol relapse. He presented with alcohol intoxication, severe abdominal pain, tachycardia, and shortness of breath. Initial evaluation revealed no acute intracranial, pulmonary, or abdominal pathology on imaging. His symptoms were attributed to alcohol withdrawal and musculoskeletal pain from a fall during intoxication. He was treated with Ativan per CIWA protocol, thiamine, folate, and multivitamins, with improvement in withdrawal symptoms. Abdominal pain was managed with oxycodone and a lidocaine patch. Tachycardia resolved and was attributed to pain and withdrawal. Asthma was controlled with nebulizers and inhalers. He remained stable, was discharged home on his prior medications, and advised to follow up with his PCP and specialist, with strong encouragement to abstain from alcohol.
